about: Topic map of the BC-only part of the AP Calculus AB and BC Course and Exam Description, in LevlPrep's own words from docs/apcalcbc-research/framework.md (CED text-verified there). No CED text is reproduced. The 81 AB topics are in docs/apcalc-ced-map.json; the BC course is both.

ced.title: AP Calculus AB and BC Course and Exam Description
ced.edition: 2019 framework, reissued effective fall 2020 (content unchanged for 2026-27)

units.title: Parametric Equations, Polar Coordinates, and Vector-Valued Functions

topics.title: Integration by Parts
objectives: Find antiderivatives and evaluate definite integrals that need integration by parts.
knowledge: Integration by parts reverses the product rule: the integral of u dv is uv minus the integral of v du.
A tabular layout is a way to organize repeated parts; graders accept it when the work is clear.

topics.title: Linear Partial Fractions
objectives: Find antiderivatives of rational functions whose denominators factor into distinct linear factors.
knowledge: A proper rational function over distinct linear factors splits into a sum of constants over each factor; each piece integrates to a logarithm.
exclusions: Repeated linear and irreducible quadratic factors (our reading of "linear, nonrepeating"; needs-author)

topics.title: Improper Integrals
objectives: Evaluate an improper integral as a limit, or show that it diverges.
knowledge: An integral is improper when a limit of integration is infinite or the integrand is unbounded on the interval.
It is evaluated as a limit of definite integrals; limit notation is kept until the limit is taken.

topics.title: Euler's Method
objectives: Approximate a point on a solution curve with Euler's method.
knowledge: Each step moves along the tangent line: the new y is the old y plus the slope times the step size.
Concavity of the solution tells whether the estimate is too high or too low.

topics.title: Logistic Models
objectives: Interpret logistic differential equations and their solutions in context without solving them.
knowledge: dy/dt = ky(a - y) says the rate is jointly proportional to the amount and to the room left below the carrying capacity a.
Solutions approach the carrying capacity; the growth rate is greatest where y is half of it.
exclusions: Solving the logistic equation explicitly is not required by the framework

topics.title: Arc Length and Distance Traveled
objectives: Find the length of a smooth planar curve y = f(x) with a definite integral.
knowledge: Arc length is the integral of the square root of 1 plus the derivative squared over the interval.

topics.title: Parametric Equations and Their Derivatives
objectives: Find the slope of a curve given by parametric equations.
knowledge: dy/dx is dy/dt divided by dx/dt, where dx/dt is not zero; it is the slope of the tangent line at that point.

topics.title: Second Derivatives of Parametric Equations
objectives: Find the second derivative of a parametric curve.
knowledge: The second derivative is the t-derivative of dy/dx divided by dx/dt, not the t-derivative of dy/dx alone.

topics.title: Arc Length of a Parametric Curve
objectives: Find the length of a parametric curve with a definite integral.
knowledge: Length is the integral over t of the square root of (dx/dt)^2 + (dy/dt)^2.

topics.title: Vector-Valued Functions and Their Derivatives
objectives: Differentiate vector-valued functions.
knowledge: A vector-valued function is differentiated component by component; the derivative of position is velocity.

topics.title: Integrating Vector-Valued Functions
objectives: Find a position from a velocity vector and an initial position.
knowledge: Integrate component by component and use the initial condition for each component.

topics.title: Motion in the Plane
objectives: Find positions, velocities, speeds and distances of a particle moving in the plane.
knowledge: Speed is the magnitude of the velocity vector.
The integral of velocity gives displacement (added to the starting position); the integral of speed gives total distance traveled.

topics.title: Polar Coordinates and Polar Derivatives
objectives: Find derivatives of polar functions and interpret them.
knowledge: With x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ, dy/dx is (dy/dθ)/(dx/dθ).
The sign of dr/dθ says whether a point on the curve moves away from or toward the origin.

topics.title: Area Inside a Polar Curve
objectives: Find the area of a region bounded by a polar curve.
knowledge: Area is one half the integral of r^2 with respect to θ over the right angles, from sectors of a circle.

topics.title: Area Between Two Polar Curves
objectives: Find the area of a region bounded by two polar curves.
knowledge: Subtract inner from outer, both squared, inside one half the integral, over the θ interval where the region lies.

topics.title: Convergent and Divergent Series
objectives: Decide whether a series converges from its partial sums.
knowledge: The nth partial sum adds the first n terms.
A series converges to S exactly when its sequence of partial sums has limit S.

topics.title: Geometric Series
objectives: Decide whether a geometric series converges and find its sum.
knowledge: A geometric series has a constant ratio r between terms; it converges when |r| < 1, to the first term over 1 - r.

topics.title: The nth Term Test for Divergence
objectives: Use the nth term test to show a series diverges.
knowledge: If the terms do not approach 0, the series diverges; terms approaching 0 prove nothing.

topics.title: The Integral Test
objectives: Use the integral test to decide convergence.
knowledge: For positive, continuous, decreasing terms, the series and the matching improper integral converge or diverge together.

topics.title: Harmonic Series and p-Series
objectives: Decide convergence of harmonic, alternating harmonic and p-series.
knowledge: A p-series converges exactly when p > 1; the harmonic series diverges; the alternating harmonic series converges.

topics.title: Comparison Tests
objectives: Use the direct and limit comparison tests to decide convergence.
knowledge: Compare positive terms with a series whose behavior is known; the limit comparison test needs a finite positive limit of the ratio of terms.

topics.title: The Alternating Series Test
objectives: Use the alternating series test to show convergence.
knowledge: An alternating series converges when its terms decrease in size and approach 0; both conditions are stated.

topics.title: The Ratio Test
objectives: Use the ratio test to decide convergence.
knowledge: If the limit of |a(n+1)/a(n)| is below 1 the series converges absolutely, above 1 it diverges, and equal to 1 the test says nothing.
exclusions: Tests other than the nth term, integral, comparison, limit comparison, alternating series and ratio tests (for example the root test) are not assessed

topics.title: Absolute and Conditional Convergence
objectives: Decide whether a series converges absolutely, conditionally or diverges.
knowledge: Absolute convergence implies convergence; a series that converges but not absolutely converges conditionally.
Rearranging an absolutely convergent series keeps its sum.

topics.title: The Alternating Series Error Bound
objectives: Bound the error of a partial sum of an alternating series.
knowledge: When the alternating series test applies, the error of a partial sum is at most the size of the first term left out.

topics.title: Taylor Polynomials
objectives: Write Taylor polynomials and use them to estimate values of a function.
knowledge: The coefficient of (x - a)^n is the nth derivative at a over n factorial.
Taylor polynomials approximate the function near the center, often better as the degree rises.

topics.title: The Lagrange Error Bound
objectives: Bound the error of a Taylor polynomial approximation.
knowledge: The Lagrange error bound uses a maximum of the next derivative on the interval; sometimes the alternating series error bound applies instead.

topics.title: Radius and Interval of Convergence
objectives: Find the radius and interval of convergence of a power series.
knowledge: The ratio test gives the radius; both endpoints are tested separately with other tests.
Term-by-term derivatives and integrals keep the radius; endpoint behavior can change.

topics.title: Taylor and Maclaurin Series
objectives: Represent a function by its Taylor or Maclaurin series and interpret it.
knowledge: A Taylor polynomial is a partial sum of the Taylor series.
The Maclaurin series of 1/(1 - x), sin x, cos x and e^x are known by heart and used to build others.

topics.title: Representing Functions as Power Series
objectives: Find a power series for a function from a known series.
knowledge: Substitute, multiply, or differentiate or integrate term by term to get a new series from a known one.

also.6.14: Selecting techniques for antidifferentiation: for BC the choice adds parts and linear partial fractions (no new learning objective).
